column3: The Aramaic refers to them by pronoun and calls the building a house; BSB names the Jews and calls the house a temple. It names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says “we said to them”; BSB says “They also asked.”
The Aramaic uses active plural subjects for not stopping them and returning a letter; BSB uses passive clauses.
The Aramaic names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says the house is being built and timber is being placed, using passives; BSB names the people as active builders.
The Aramaic calls the building a house; BSB calls it a temple.
The Aramaic says the name of the men at their heads, with name singular; BSB uses names of their leaders.
The Aramaic calls the building a house; BSB calls it a temple.

The Aramaic repeats Cyrus and king; BSB combines these references into one named subject.
The Aramaic uses a passive for the articles being given to Sheshbazzar; BSB makes King Cyrus the active giver.
The Aramaic includes “go” and “bring them down”; BSB says “put them.” It says “its place”; BSB says “its original site.”
The Aramaic calls the archive the king’s house of treasures; BSB says “royal archives.”
